manage_providers.description: An org owner or instance admin: may set up providers and manage every vault's references.

manage_refs.description: May manage references at all (an org manager, or the owner of a vault).

toggle_helper.description: An instance admin: may switch the secrets helper on or off.

vaults.description: The vaults the caller may bind references to.

snapshot.description:
Who had access to what when the review started: `people`, each with `spaces`, `tokens`,
`apps` and `sessions`.

undecided.description: People nobody has decided about yet.

you.description: The caller: they cannot decide about themselves.

AccessReview.description: A review with its snapshot and decisions.

detail.description:
The event's detail as written (`result=<hash> keep=.. remove=.. suspend=.. not_reviewed=..`).
Its SHA-256 is the event's `detail_digest` in the chain.

AccessReviewDecision.description: A person's decision in a review.

note.description: Why, in a sentence (optional, at most 500 characters).

AccessReviewExport.description:
A completed review as a file: the snapshot, the decisions, both hashes and the security log
event that recorded the completion.

oneOf.description: The completion's place in the hash-chained security log, once sealed.

chain_matches.description:
True when the chained completion event commits to this review as it is now: its detail
names this `result` document's hash and the chain holds that detail's plain SHA-256. False
means the review was changed after it was completed (even if `result_hash` was recomputed).
The offline verifier checks the same: `verify-audit-export.py LOG.json --review THIS.json`.

result.description: The document `result_hash` is the SHA-256 of (canonical JSON: keys sorted, no spaces).

result_hash_matches.description: True when `result` still hashes to the `result_hash` recorded at completion.

snapshot.description: Who had access to what at the start; `snapshot_hash` is its SHA-256 (canonical JSON).

acked.description: Ids that were leased and are now done. Ids that are unknown, already done or not leased are skipped.

code.description:
The stable code when the secrets helper itself failed: `helper_disabled` or `helper_unreachable`
(on `secret.resolve` rows of op:// and bws:// references; never on an eu:// handle).

lineage.description: For a transform: the held secrets it was derived from; for an outbound call: the host.

reference.description: The reference or handle concerned (for a request, the handle it will fill).

ActivityRow.description: A row of the person's own activity about their data.

admin.description: `true` makes the person an admin, `false` takes admin rights away.

Agg.description: How a metric combines its entities' values.

AmbiguousTarget.description:
A link column's value that names two or more entities in the vault: skipped, never guessed, until a
person merges them (`entity_merge`) or the column is mapped another way.

kinds.description: The kind of each entity it names.

AuditCategory.description: Which kind of event a filter chip asks for.

AuditChainBreak.description: Where and how a chain stops verifying.

kind.description:
`altered` (an event's content no longer matches its hash), `link` (an event does not
follow the one before it), `missing` (events are gone), `duplicate`, `head` (the newest
event is not the recorded head), `checkpoint` (a checkpoint disagrees with its event) or
`genesis`.

seq.description: The sequence number where the chain stops verifying, when there is one.

AuditCheckpoint.description: A point a verifier can start from or compare against.

kind.description:
`genesis` (the chain's start, seq 0), `retention` (the last event the retention window
deleted), `periodic` (a copy of the head) or `export` (written into an export file).

pruned.description: For `retention`: how many events that cut deleted.

AuditEventFields.description: The fields one event's hash covers, in their canonical form.

AuditExport.description:
An offline-verifiable slice of one ledger. Metadata only: no memory text, chat content,
prompts, secrets or free-text detail (the detail is committed by its hash).

oneOf.description: The point the first event hangs from: its sequence minus one and its `prev_hash`.

checkpoints.description: Stored checkpoints inside the range, plus one every 1000 events and one at the last event.

from.description: The requested range, RFC 3339; empty when open.

oneOf.description: The ledger's head when the export was made.

ok.description: The server's own check of the events in this file.

range.description:
The file's own range: its first and last event, the ledger's head when it was made, and how
many events were still unsealed (written, not yet in the chain) and so are not in it. The
offline verifier checks it against the events and the head.

truncated.description: True when the range held more than one export carries; `next_seq` is where to resume.

version.description: The canonical form the hashes use (`eunomia.audit.v1`).

AuditExportEvent.description: One event in an export: its canonical fields (the detail only as its hash) and stored hash.

AuditVerification.description: The result of walking one ledger.

oneOf.description: The checkpoint the walk started from (the genesis, or the last retention cut).

before_chain.description: For the `instance` ledger: events written before the chain started, which have no hash.

oneOf.description: The first break, if any.

checked.description: Events whose hash and link were checked.

detail_unchecked.description:
Events whose detail could not be checked against its digest because the encryption key
changed since they were written (their hash and link were still checked).

ok.description: True when every stored event verified from the anchor to the head.

pending.description: Events written but not sealed yet (sealed by the next replay).

ledgers.description:
The workspace's own ledger first, then, for a server operator (or any admin while the
install has one workspace), the `instance` ledger: events with no workspace, such as sign-ins
with an unknown email.

can_manage_org.description: May invite people to the organisation and see its seats (an owner or admin of it, or an instance admin).

has_password.description: False for an account made by an OpenID Connect provider: it has no password to change or use.

is_admin.description: True for an instance admin: the first user, or an email in `EUNOMIA_ADMIN_EMAILS`.

oidc_provider.description: The display name of the configured OpenID Connect provider when this account can sign in with it.

org_role.description: The account's role in its organisation: `owner`, `admin` or `member`.

AutomapBody.description: What to auto-map: synced records (all, one source or one record type) or an uploaded CSV.

oneOf.description: The server's model proposed; `ontology` is the vault's ontology after the proposals.

skipped.description: Model items left out for an unknown record type, an invalid name or field.

oneOf.description: No server model (or it failed): read `profiles` and `key_matches` and call `ontology_propose`.

BadCell.description: A row or cell that was not imported.

column.description: The column, or none when the whole row was left out.

line.description: The file's line (the header is line 1).

auth_mode.description: Which sign-in methods the login and register pages offer.

oidc_provider.description: The button label ("Continue with {oidc_provider}") when an OpenID Connect provider is configured.

args.description: Tool arguments, or `{method, uri, body}` for a route. Secrets are masked.

name.description: The tool name, or `METHOD /matched/route` for a route.

source.description: The raw error text. Never sent to ordinary clients; admins only.

truncated.description: True when `args` was cut to fit the size cap (not replayable).

user.description: The caller's record id, if the request was authenticated.

Change.description: One row of a vault's change log.

actor.description: Who wrote it: a user, token or OAuth client id, or `system`.

id.description: The item's id; fetch it to see what changed (it may be gone).

op.description: `created`, `updated`, `deleted` or `merged` (an entity merged into another, which gets `updated`).

seq.description: Strictly increasing per vault, with no gaps.

ChangePage.description: A page of changes and the cursor for the next one.

next.description: Pass as `after` next time: the last seq returned, or the `after` given when there was none.

error.description:
`denied`, `provider_error` or `bad_config` when not ok. (The sidecar itself not answering is a
`secret.unavailable` error with reason `helper_disabled` or `helper_unreachable`, not this.)

ChunkRef.description: Where one chunk sits in its document.

char_start.description: Character offsets of the chunk in the extracted text, end exclusive.

chunk_id.description: The chunk's record id for `get` (also its vector's reference).

lease_secs.description:
How long the batch is yours, 5 to 3600 seconds; default 300. Ack or nack before it runs out,
or the events go to the next claim.

events.description: Oldest first. Empty when nothing is waiting.

vault_id.description: The extension's target vault, to pass as `vault_id` to the tools; `null` is your personal vault.

ids.description: ids of points returned by the cloud, at most 40

vault_ids.description: the vaults the points were listed from (same as `vault_ids` of the cloud); default: your personal vault

code.description: A six-digit authenticator code, or (where a recovery code is accepted) a recovery code.

ColumnPlan.description: How one column would be imported.

link.description: The approved link type whose targets it names ("supplied_by supplier"), alongside any property.

property.description: The property it feeds, from its `source_map`.

ColumnUse.description: One column of an import: the property it wrote, or why it was left out.

link.description: The link type whose targets it named ("supplied_by supplier").

label.description: A name for the new connection, for example the account's email address or the device's name.

ConnectorOut.description:
One connection. A user may connect the same kind more than once (two Gmail accounts); each
connection has its own credentials, sync and records.

id.description: The connection's id (`connector:...`). Routes taking `{connector}` accept it.

label.description: The name the user gave this connection (an email address, a device name); "" if none.

routing.description: Which vault its syncs file records in: a default destination and ordered rules.

routing_fields.description: The fields this connector's rules can match on.

source_key.description:
This connection's key in `GET /api/sources` and `POST /api/sources/{key}/sync`: the source key for
a kind's first connection, `{source}~{instance}` for each one added after it.

oneOf.description:
Replaces the routing (destination vault and rules). It applies to records synced from now on;
`POST /api/connectors/{connector}/move` re-files those already synced.

mfa_code.description:
A current authenticator or recovery code, when your account has two-step verification and its last
second factor is older than 10 minutes (`auth.step_up_required`). Only needed to approve.

loopback.description: True when the redirect goes to this computer only (localhost); the page warns about it.

redirect_host.description: Host the user is sent back to after deciding.

redirect_to.description: Send the browser here: the client's redirect URI with the code (or the denial).

vault_id.description: A vault you belong to; omit for your personal vault.

Datatype.description: What a property's values are. A datatype, not a business field: the vault says which property has it.

chunks.description: Chunks removed from retrieval, and memories that had been extracted from them.

text.description: The extracted text of the current revision (up to `max_chars`; `text_truncated` says when cut).

max_bytes.description: The largest upload accepted, in bytes.

storage.description: Whether this server stores documents at all (`EUNOMIA_DOCUMENTS_BACKEND` is set).

DocumentOut.description: One document as callers see it.

download_url.description: Authenticated `GET` for the original bytes (same credentials as this call).

error.description: Why indexing failed. Absent otherwise (a tool result with an `error` key reads as a failed call).

revision.description: Bumped by a re-upload or a re-index; chunks name the revision they came from.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the original bytes, hex.

status.description: `indexing`, `ready` or `failed` (`deleted` only while a deletion's cleanup is unfinished).

vault.description: The vault (memory space) the document is in.

password.description:
Your account password: setting up an authenticator from Settings needs it, so a stolen session alone
cannot put an attacker's authenticator on the account.

me.description: The signed-in user (the session cookie is set with this answer).

recovery_codes.description: Shown once. Each works once, in place of an authenticator code.

Enrolment.description: What the enrolment screen shows, once.

qr_svg.description: The QR code as a standalone SVG document (no scripts), for an `` tag.

secret.description: The secret in base32, for typing into an authenticator app by hand. Shown only now.

EntityCreated.description:
The entity a create found or made. `kind_mapped` is set when the vault's owners rejected the kind
asked for and the entity went to its merge target instead.

properties.description: The current value of each approved property of its kind that it has.

close_workspace.description:
You confirm that a workspace whose only member you are is closed with your account (everything
in it is deleted). Without it such a request is refused with `subject.workspace_closes`.

mfa_code.description:
With two-step verification on: a code from your authenticator, unless you signed in with one in
the last 10 minutes (`auth.step_up_required` otherwise).

password.description: Your password, typed again. Required when the account has one.

close_workspace.description: Confirms closing any workspace whose only member the person is.

mfa_code.description:
With two-step verification on for your account: a code from your authenticator, unless you
signed in with one in the last 10 minutes (`auth.step_up_required` otherwise).

password.description:
Your own password, typed again (an operator who signs in only with single sign-on confirms with a
sign-in from the last 10 minutes instead).

ErasureRecord.description:
The record a completed erasure leaves, for the People page (no personal data: an opaque reference,
per-category counts, the post-check result and the review counts).

counts.description: Rows removed or anonymised per category.

deleting_at.description: When it took its first irreversible step; none while it can still be cancelled.

post_check.description: Rows still naming the person per table after the erasure: every value is 0 when it passed.

requested_by.description: `self`, `operator` or `reapply` (a restore brought the person back and they were erased again).

review.description: Mentions of the person's email left in content other people wrote, for review.

subject_ref.description: The keyed hash of the erased account's id (never the id or the email).

ErasureTicket.description: An erasure as the routes report it.

EventOut.description: A claimed event, for the consumer.

attempts.description: How many times this event has been handed out, this claim included.

body.description: The delivery's JSON body, as sent.

delivery_id.description: The sender's delivery id (`X-Delivery-Id`, `X-GitHub-Delivery` or `Idempotency-Key`), or one we made up.

id.description: `extension_event:...`; pass it back to ack or nack.

ExportRow.description: What the exports list shows (never the archive).

scope.description: `self` (the person's own, every workspace) or `organisation` (an admin's, one workspace).

claimed.description: Leased to a consumer right now.

dead.description: Handed out five times without an ack, or nacked at the last attempt (kept 30 days).

done.description: Acked, until they are pruned (7 days).

pending.description: Waiting to be claimed, counting events whose lease ran out.

secret_hint.description: The last four characters of the current secret.

vault_id.description:
The vault the script is expected to write to; `null` is your personal vault. Informational:
the script passes it as `vault_id` to the tools.

ExtensionWithSecret.description: The only response that carries a secret in the clear.

secret.description:
Shown once. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`, or sign the body with it
(`X-Eunomia-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`). Rotate to get a new one.

FieldProfile.description: One field of one record type, from a sample.

date_format.description: For dates: the notation the values are written in, such as `YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD/MM/YYYY`.

distinct_count.description: Distinct values in the sample, counted up to 26 (26 means 26 or more).

enum_values.description: Every distinct value, for an enum candidate (25 or fewer).

is_unique.description: Every sampled value differs (and there is at least one).

null_rate.description: The share of sampled records with no value here (missing, null or blank), 0 to 1.

path.description: The payload key path (`billing.country`) or the CSV column.

top_values.description: The commonest values, most frequent first, at most five.

FillBody.description: What the pop-up sends. `value` is zeroised when this is dropped; Debug never prints it.

allowed_hosts.description: The hosts it may be sent to (defaults to what the agent asked for).

any_agent.description: Let any credential of a vault member use it, not only the one that asked.

placements.description: `header`, `query`, `body` (defaults to what the agent asked for).

value.description: The secret. Write-only: encrypted at once, never returned, logged or shown again.

Filter.description: Keeps entities whose value of `property` compares to `value` by `op` (`in` takes a list).

value.description: In the property's datatype; a list for `in`.

HeldOut.description: A held secret as listed. Never its value or ciphertext.

derived_from.description: The held secrets it was derived from (empty for a pasted one).

configured.description: `false`: there is no updater on this server (no `update-status/`); switch the profile on by hand.

HelperStatus.description: The secrets helper's status for Settings.

can_request.description:
The updater's request channel is there (`update-status/`): "Enable password managers" works.
When `false`, Settings shows the manual steps instead.

enabled.description: The profile is on for this backend (`EUNOMIA_COMPOSE_PROFILES` names `secrets`).

message.description: Why, for people (the updater's error, or why the helper is not answering).

pending.description: `enable` or `disable` while a request waits for the updater.

profile.description: The compose profile to switch on by hand: `secrets`.

reason.description:
`helper_disabled` (off or starting) or `helper_unreachable` (unreachable): what a resolution
gets now; absent when running.

state.description:
`off` (the `secrets` profile is not on), `starting` (asked for, or started and not answering yet),
`running` (answers its health check) or `unreachable` (on, but not answering).

hold.description: `true` places a legal hold (the account cannot be erased), `false` lifts it.

erasure_open.description:
An erasure of this account is open. A hold placed now parks it (`held`) before its next
irreversible step; lifting the hold resumes it.

legal_hold_at.description: When the hold was placed, RFC 3339; none when there is no hold.

status.description: `accepted`, or `duplicate` when this delivery id was already stored.

requested.description: Present only when the updater is configured.

HttpsRequest.description: Body of `POST /https`: turn HTTPS on for a domain, or off.

domain.description: A public DNS name (eunomia.example.com). Required when enabling.

email.description: Contact address for Let's Encrypt. Required when enabling.

HttpsStatus.description:
Documents `GET /https/status`. The handler merges the updater's
`https-status.json`, so everything except `configured` is absent when the
updater is not configured.

ids.description: Event ids from a claim, at most 500.

ImportBody.description: How to import a CSV's rows: the approved kind, the naming column, and optionally which column feeds which property.

ambiguous.description: Link column values that name more than one entity, skipped.

bad.description: Rows and cells left out, at most 100 listed.

created.description: Entities made by this run, and ones it found and updated.

linked.description: Relations this run wrote (a re-run writes none), and the link targets it created by name.

reused.description:
Link targets that already existed in another kind (an organisation a supplier column names),
linked to instead of a new entity.

skipped.description: Names skipped because their kind was rejected and has no existing approved replacement.

values.description: Values written (each new or updated in place).

kind.description: The kind its mapped properties belong to, once auto-mapping proposed them.

oneOf.description: That kind's review status; none when it was never reviewed.

name_column.description: The column that names each row's entity: the first one no property or link is mapped from.

ready.description: The kind is approved and at least one mapped property is: `document_import_rows` will run.

InferredType.description:
What a field's values look like. The datatypes of a property, plus `id` for a key that names a
record (a link candidate).

change_log_behind.description: True when the counter is behind the log (the next write's append would collide).

change_log_top.description: Highest seq in the change log, and the counter the next write continues from.

dangling_memories.description: Memories whose subject entity no longer exists.

misfiled_memories.description: Memories filed here whose subject is in another vault (not repaired automatically).

ok.description: True when nothing below needs attention.

oneOf.description: Set on a repair: what it removed or fixed.

InvitationAccepted.description: What accepting while signed in did.

already_member.description:
The account was already in the organisation; the invitation is now used up (an admin invitation
made a member an admin).

role.description: The role the account holds in the organisation now: `owner`, `admin` or `member`.

InvitationLookup.description: What the invitation page shows before anyone accepts.

email.description: The invited email: the account that accepts must have this one.

org_name.description:
The organisation's name as its admins chose it (not verified by anyone); empty for a personal
workspace, whose name is its founder's email and is not shown.

personal.description: The invitation is to someone's personal workspace (its name is not shown).

invited_by.description:
Email of the space's owner when it has exactly one: only owners invite, so that is who sent it.
None when there are several owners (or it is unknown); show "Someone" then.

token.description: The token from the invitation link (the part after `#`).

vault.description: The new vault holding this Eunomia's copy.

name.description: How the other Eunomia will name this one (default: `EUNOMIA_INSTANCE_NAME`, else your email).

KeyMatch.description: One key field whose values are another record type's ids.

values.description: Distinct values checked, and how many match.

Kind.description:
One provider kind and what Settings says about it. The one source of truth for the kinds, their
names and their stability (the settings API serves it; the UI and the docs follow it).

kind.description: As stored and as the sidecar names it.

note.description: One line for Settings when the kind is in preview.

oneOf.description: Writes under the kind go to `merge_into` from now on; without it they are refused.
Set or (blank) clear the description; the status stays as it is.

KindItem.description: One entity kind of the vault.

entities.description: Entities of this kind in the vault.

merge_into.description: Rejected: where writes under this kind go instead. Proposed: the merge the proposer suggests.

metrics.description: Its metrics, each with its review status and expression. Only an approved one runs by name.

oneOf.description: Who proposed it; none for a kind that was never reviewed.

properties.description: Its typed properties, each with its review status. Only an approved one takes values.

synonyms.description: Other names written in the vault's data for this kind.

KindMapped.description: A write under a rejected kind that went to its merge target instead.

LinkCheck.description: A link the model proposed, after the value check.

ambiguous.description: Values that name two or more entities: an import skips them until they are merged.

kept.description: Proposed (some values match) or dropped (none do).

reason.description: The match share in words, as the link's proposal reason says it.

reused.description:
Values that name an existing entity of another kind (an organisation a supplier column names):
an import links to it instead of making a new one. They count as matched.

skipped.description: Names whose rejected kind has no existing approved replacement.

password.description: The existing account's password: proves it is yours, and links without removing anything.

start_fresh.description:
`true`: you don't know the password. A new, empty account is made for you; the existing one is set
aside (suspended, nothing of it inherited) for a server operator to review, restore or erase.

mfa.description:
Set when the password was right but the account's second step comes first: `verify` (enter the
account's authenticator code) or `enrol` (this server requires two-step verification: set it up).
No session and no link yet; the response sets the short-lived second-step cookie, and the link is
made when that step passes.

started_fresh.description: A new account was made and the existing one set aside.

email.description: The address both the provider and the existing account have.

LinkItem.description: One link type of the vault: relations labelled `label` from a `from_kind` entity to a `to_kind` one.

count.description: Relations of this type in the vault.

source_map.description:
The record fields or CSV columns that name each relation's target, from auto-mapping: a CSV
import finds or creates the entity a cell names and writes the relation.

code.description: The stable code when the secrets helper itself failed: `helper_disabled` or `helper_unreachable`.

ref_id.description: `credential_ref:...`, empty when the reference was not registered.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

MappedType.description: What became of one record type.

unmapped.description: Fields no property took (left out by the model, or claimed by an earlier property).

redacted.description:
Secrets this write replaced with `[redacted: <kind>]` markers (kind and count only). Present
only on a write or edit that redacted something.

entities.description: Entities in the merged vault (duplicates across the two sources count once).

oneOf.description: The metric runs by name from now on. Its properties must be approved first.

Runs of the metric go to `merge_into` (a metric of the same kind) from now on; without it they
are refused.
Set or (blank) clear the description; the status stays as it is.

MetricExpr.description:
What a metric computes, over the latest value of each property per entity. Never query text: an
unknown field is refused.

filters.description: ANDed, and on a ratio applied to both sides.

oneOf.description: Ratio only.

property.description:
The measured property: needed by sum, avg, min, max and count_distinct; count counts the
entities that have it, or every entity without it.

oneOf.description:
Instead of a property: a value worked out per entity, such as stock × cost (sum, avg, min and
max only).

time_property.description: A date or datetime property a series groups the entities by.

MetricItem.description: One metric of a kind, as the ontology view shows it. Its value is never here: `metric_eval` runs it.

expr_words.description: The expression in plain words, e.g. "Sum of price where status is late".

merge_into.description: Rejected: the metric of the same kind that runs instead. Proposed: the merge the proposer suggests.

open_org_handles.description: Org database handles currently open in this process (the pool is capped).

queries_without_org_context.description:
Queries that ran without an org context since the process started: an unknown or unready org
asked for, or a statement that reached for the other database's tables. Must stay 0; each one
is also logged at error level.

MfaPendingOut.description:
A correct password whose sign-in still needs its second step. No session yet: the response sets a
short-lived cookie that only the `/api/auth/mfa/challenge/*` routes accept.

mfa_required.description:
`verify`: enter an authenticator or recovery code. `enrol`: this server requires two-step
verification and the account has none yet, so set up an authenticator first.

available.description: False for an account that signs in only through single sign-on: the provider handles its second factor.

enabled.description: Two-step verification is on for this account.

required.description: An admin requires two-step verification for every password account on this server.

unreadable.description:
True when the stored authenticator can no longer be read (`ENCRYPTION_KEY` changed): sign in with a
recovery code, turn it off and set it up again.

left.description: Facts and relations left in a vault the owner is no longer a member of.

memories.description: Facts drawn from them that moved too (one the destination already had is not duplicated).

records.description: Records re-filed to the vault the current rules route them to.

relations.description: Relations drawn from them that moved too.

error.description: Why, kept on the event (500 characters).

dead.description: Handed out five times already, so dead-lettered instead.

warning.description: Set on `/readyz` when the server is up but running on the public empty `ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

kinds.description: The built-in kinds first, then the others by name.

strict.description:
"Only approved kinds and links": a write under a custom kind or a relation under a link type
that is not approved is refused and filed as a proposal.

OrgInvitation.description: An open invitation, as an org admin sees it. Never carries the token.

expired.description: The link has expired; resend it to make a new one.

invited_by.description: The email of the admin who sent it.

sent_at.description: When the current link was made (a resend makes a new one).

role.description: `member` (default) or `admin` (can invite people and see seats; not an instance admin).

OrgInvitationLink.description: A new or resent invitation, with its link. The link is shown once: only its hash is kept.

link.description: `<frontend>/invite#<token>`. The token rides in the fragment, which browsers never send to a server.

token.description: The token alone, for clients that build their own link.

OrgSeats.description: OrgSeats for one org (the hosted business bills on these). Counts only.

active_members.description: Members whose account is not suspended.

pending_invitations.description: Open invitations that have not expired.

Origin.description: Who proposed a row: the server's model, an agent over MCP, or a person in the app.

enabled.description: `false` makes the inbox answer 403 `extension.disabled`; buffered events stay.

vault_id.description: A vault you belong to; an empty string goes back to your personal vault; omit to keep it.

address.description: The address that answered last (a guest's view of its host).

digests_match.description: Whether both copies held the same items at the last check (`None`: not checked yet).

direction.description: `host`: this Eunomia holds the original and shares it out; `guest`: this is a copy of another's.

role.description: What the guest may do: `edit` or `read`.

addresses.description: The addresses a new code would carry, best first.

codes.description: Codes made for this vault and not used yet (owners only; empty for members).

links.description: Other Eunomias this vault is shared with (or copied from).

PendingInviteOut.description: An invitation into a vault that the invitee has not answered yet, as its owners see it.

admin.description:
Why this person is an admin: `creator` (the first account), `operator` (listed in the server's
admin emails), `granted` (made an admin in the app), or empty for a member.

is_you.description: The admin looking at the list.

last_active.description: Latest browser session activity or API token use, RFC 3339; none if never seen.

legal_hold_at.description: When an admin placed a legal hold on the account, RFC 3339; none when there is none. A held account cannot be erased.

mfa.description:
Two-step verification: `on`, `off`, or `provider` for an account that signs in only through single
sign-on (its identity provider handles the second factor).

shared_spaces.description: Shared spaces this person is an active member of (their personal space not counted).

suspended_at.description: When an admin suspended the account, RFC 3339; none while it is active.

tokens.description: How many API tokens this person holds (see `/api/admin/people/{user_id}/tokens`).

workspace_owner.description:
The workspace's owner (one per workspace). An owner whose workspace has other members hands it
over (`/api/admin/people/{user_id}/workspace-owner`) before their account can be erased.

expires_at.description: `null` for a token that never expires.

reason.description: A stable machine-readable reason under `code`, when there is one (docs/errors.md).

oneOf.description:
Values for the property go to `merge_into` (a property of the same kind) from now on; without
it they are refused.
Set or (blank) clear the description; the status stays as it is.

PropertyItem.description: One property of a kind, as the ontology view shows it.

merge_into.description: Rejected: the property of the same kind its values go to. Proposed: the merge the proposer suggests.

samples.description: A few of them, as text with their unit.

source_map.description: The record fields or CSV columns it was mapped from.

values.description: Values written for it in the vault, history included.

PropertyValue.description: One property's current value on an entity.

as_of.description: When the value was true, RFC 3339.

source.description: The synced record it came from.

unit.description: The value's unit, else the property's.

value.description: A number, a bool or a string (a date is YYYY-MM-DD, a datetime RFC 3339).

ProposedKind.description:
A proposed kind after the call: `status` is the row's, so a kind a person already decided shows
that decision (the proposal did not change it).

ProposedMetric.description: A proposed metric after the call, with the row's status (a decided one keeps its decision).

ProposedProperty.description: A proposed property after the call, with the row's status (a decided one keeps its decision).

host.description:
Connect: the Connect server URL (required). Bitwarden: the server URL (optional; the US cloud when
empty, `https://vault.bitwarden.eu` for the EU cloud). Service accounts: none.

token.description: The bootstrap token. Required when none is stored; omit to keep the stored one. Write-only.

ProviderOut.description: A configured provider. Never the token: only that one is stored.

configured.description: Always `true` in a listed row: a token is stored (encrypted). It is never returned.

host.description: The server URL; shown to org managers only (a vault owner sees `null`).

preview.description: `true` for a kind in preview (Bitwarden Secrets Manager).

blockers.description: What stops the vault answering numbers, each in one sentence, for the owner.

ready.description:
No blockers: nothing proposed is waiting, a metric is approved, and every property an approved
metric reads is approved and has values.

strict.description: Whether the vault takes only approved kinds and links.

queued.description: Erasures queued again: accounts a restore brought back, and restored rows whose owner was erased.

paths_truncated.description: More fields than [`MAX_PATHS`]: the later ones were left out.

recovery_codes.description: Shown once. Each works once, in place of an authenticator code.

Redaction.description: What one write had redacted: `count` secrets of `kind` (e.g. "github token").

dry_run.description: Only count what would be replaced (the default); `false` deletes it and queues extraction again.

ReextractOut.description:
What a re-extract run replaces: the connection's live records, the facts and relations drawn from
them, and the observations resting only on those facts.

allowed_actors.description: `user:...`, `api_token:...` or `oauth_client:...`; empty: any member of the vault.

allowed_tools.description: Tools that may resolve it; `*` is any tool that takes secrets.

provider.description: The provider kind that resolves it. Ignored on update.

vault_id.description: The vault the reference is bound to: only its members may use it.

invitation.description:
The token from an organisation invitation link. The account joins that organisation, and a valid
invitation is the permission to sign up even when `SIGNUP` is `invite` or `closed`. The email must be the invited one.

removed_derived.description: How many secrets derived from the old value were deleted.

from.description: Vaults connectors may name now (e.g. the two vaults just merged).

to.description: The vault to name instead (e.g. the merged vault).

connectors.description: Connectors whose default or rules changed.

RequestOut.description: A request as the pop-up and the Connectors page show it. Never a value.

can_fill.description: The signed-in person may paste the value (they asked, it is pending).

ReusedTarget.description:
An entity that already existed under a link column's value, in another kind than the link's
target: linked to as it is, never retyped and never duplicated.

default_vault.description: Where records no rule matches go (`vault:...`); absent: your personal vault.

rules.description: Checked in order; the first match wins.

RowExpr.description:
A value worked out for each entity before the metric combines them, such as stock × cost: two
terms and an operation, nested at most [`MAX_ROW_DEPTH`] deep. Typed data, never query text.

RowOp.description: How a row expression combines two values of one entity.

RowTerm.description: One side of a row expression: a number, a property of the kind, or another row expression.

value.description: What the field must be (case-insensitive); for `title`, a word or phrase it contains.

vault.description: The vault a matching record goes to (`vault:...`).

mfa_code.description:
A current authenticator or recovery code, when your own account has two-step verification and its
last second factor is older than 10 minutes (`auth.step_up_required`).

require_mfa.description:
Every password account on this server, in every organisation, must pass two-step verification before
it gets a session. Accounts that sign in through single sign-on are left to the identity provider
unless they set up their own authenticator.

updated_by.description: Email of the operator who last changed it.

without_mfa.description:
Active password accounts on the whole server (every organisation) without two-step verification yet:
while it is required they are signed out and must set it up at their next sign-in.

current.description: This is the session the request itself is using.

model_configured.description: A usable model endpoint resolves for this user (their key, the server's, or a keyless local endpoint): chat can answer.

sync_check_connectivity.description:
Probe for an internet connection before a scheduled sync and skip it quietly while offline.
Default true. "Sync now" reports `status: "offline"` instead of failing.

sync_intervals.description: Open map of source key to sync interval seconds.

owner_name.description: The user's own name, used by email extraction so facts about the mailbox owner have a subject ("" = unknown)

sync_check_connectivity.description: Skip scheduled syncs while there is no internet connection (default true).

addresses.description: The addresses in the code, best first.

code.description: Send this to the person running the other Eunomia. It works once.

fingerprint.description: This instance's fingerprint, to compare by eye.

expires_in_hours.description: How long the code works, in hours (default 168, at most 720).

role.description: `read` by default. Explicit `edit` lets the other Eunomia add and change.

SignInOut.description: What login and register answer: the signed-in user, or the second step still to do.

allowlist.description: The emails that may sign up when `mode` is `invite`. Empty unless you are the server's operator.

operators.description: Emails the server lists as admins (`EUNOMIA_ADMIN_EMAILS`). Empty unless you are the server's operator.

Similarity.description:
Pairwise relationships between points of the cloud, measured on the real vectors (not the 3D
projection). Row `i` / column `j` of every matrix refers to `ids[i]` / `ids[j]`.

correlation.description: Pearson correlation of the vectors' components, -1..1

SkippedTarget.description: A name whose rejected kind cannot be reused.

SnapshotOut.description: Each side is null when that connector is not connected or its call failed.

SourceField.description:
A record field or CSV column a property's values come from: `source` and `record_type` name the
records (`stripe`, `stripe.charge`), or `document` and the document id for an uploaded CSV, and
`path` the payload key path or the column.

SourceOut.description:
One connection of a source. A kind's first connection keeps the source key as its `key`; each one
added after it is `{source}~{instance}`.

account.description: The name the user gave the connection; "" if none.

connector.description: The connection's id (`connector:...`); absent for a source never set up.

Stability.description:
How far a provider kind is proven. `Preview`: works against our mock of the provider's API, not yet
checked against the provider's own service; shown with a "Preview" badge in Settings.

invitation.description: The token from the organisation invitation link.

next.description: Same-site path to open after sign-in (the invitation page).

Status.description: What a person decided about a kind or link, as stored.

StatusCounts.description: Rows of one sort, by status.

observed.description: In use but never reviewed (kinds and link types only).

can_require.description: You may require two-step verification for the whole server (`/api/admin/security`): the server's operator.

oneOf.description: Instead of a property: a value worked out per entity (sum, avg, min and max only).
The server's model proposed; `ontology` is the vault's ontology after the proposals.

skipped.description: Model proposals left out for an invalid name or field.

oneOf.description: No server model (or it failed): review `profile` yourself and call `ontology_propose`.

SyncReport.description:
Outcome of a sync or webhook ingest: an ingest report, `source` + `error` when the sync failed, or
`status: "already_running"` when a sync of that source is already queued or running, or
`status: "queued"` when it was queued but no worker finished it within the wait. Schema only:
the handlers pass the report through.

status.description: `partial`, `already_running`, `queued`, or `offline` (the connectivity check found no internet; nothing was attempted).

error.description: Present only when the ping failed with an error.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in the future. Omit for 90 days. Explicit null never expires.

mfa_code.description:
A current authenticator or recovery code. Needed from a browser session of an account with
two-step verification when its last second factor is older than 10 minutes (`auth.step_up_required`).

scopes.description:
Any of `memory:read`, `memory:write`, `vaults:admin`, `connectors`. Defaults
to read and write memory when omitted or null. Cannot exceed the creating credential's own scopes.

vault_id.description:
Omit for your Personal space. Explicit null allows all your spaces.
A string restricts the token to one vault you belong to.

expires_at.description: `null` for a token that never expires.

name.description: The new name: trimmed, 1 to 80 characters.

scope.description: `org`: everyone in the org (instance admin). `self`: the caller's own usage.

series_step.description: `hour` for ranges up to 48 hours, `day` beyond.

email.description: An active member who becomes an owner; the caller becomes a member.

requested.description: Present only when the updater is configured.

UpdateStatus.description:
Documents the body of `GET /update/status`. The handler merges the on-disk
`status.json` written by `scripts/auto-update.sh` verbatim, so every field
except `configured` is absent when the updater is not configured.

progress.description: While `applying`: what the updater is waiting on (e.g. a slow first boot it keeps retrying).

credential_id.description: The token's or OAuth client's id; empty for the browser session.

kind.description: `session` (the signed-in browser), `token` (personal API token) or `oauth` (an OAuth client).

label.description: Token name, OAuth client name, or "Browser session".

session.description: The `Mcp-Session-Id` the client sent, or the chat thread id.

UsageCounts.description: Calls, failed calls and mean duration of a group of tool calls.

avg_ms.description: Mean time a call took, in milliseconds.

errors.description: Calls that ended in an error (a tool error value, a refused scope, or a failure).

bucket.description: Start of the hour or day (UTC), RFC 3339.

matches.description: True when both copies hold exactly the same items.

remote_digest.description: The other side's digest: asked just now (guest), or as of its last exchange (host).

ViewStatus.description: A kind or link as the ontology view shows it. `Observed`: used in the vault, never reviewed.

WebhookOut.description:
Body of the webhook route: `{"status": "ignored"}` or an ingest report with
`status: "ok"`. Schema only.

action.description: The raw action code, such as `vault.invite`.

actor_email.description: The person who acted; for a failed sign-in, the email that was tried. Empty for the system.

outcome.description: `ok`, or the code that ended the action.

reason.description:
Why a failed action failed, in words ("Already a member or invited, or no account has that email").
Empty when it worked, or when `summary` already says why.

result.description: The outcome in words: "Done", "Not allowed", "Declined", "Refused" or "Failed".

summary.description: What happened, in plain words ("Invited user@acme.test to acme-engineering").

via.description: How they acted: empty for the browser, `API token`, `app` (an OAuth client) or `system`.
